title: Cost-Effective Microsoft Places Alternatives for Desk Booking
summary: Microsoft Places desk booking, autorelease, and occupancy reports need paid space licenses. Compare cost-effective alternatives that work in Slack and Teams.
body_markdown:
Microsoft Places looks like a free add-on if you're already paying for Microsoft 365 or Teams. It isn't, not once you need actual desk booking.


## What Microsoft Places Really Costs You


Core Places features, like workplace presence and basic room booking, come with plans such as Microsoft 365 Business Standard, E3, E5, or a standalone Teams license. No extra charge there.


But the features most hybrid teams actually need cost more:


- **Individual desk booking** requires a separate "space license" (Microsoft Teams Shared Space or Shared Space – Single Space).
- **Autorelease** , which frees up desks nobody checked into, needs that same paid license.
- **Occupancy analytics** , the reporting that tells you whether your office is actually being used, is locked behind a space license too.
- **AI-assisted booking** needs a Microsoft Copilot license on top of everything else.


So the "included" tool turns into a stack of per-space add-ons once you want it to do the job. For a 200-desk office, that adds up fast, and it's easy to lose track of what you're paying for across licenses.


## What to Look for in a Cheaper, Simpler Alternative


Before you commit to untangling Microsoft's licensing tiers, it's worth asking what you actually need:


- **Desk and hot-desk booking** that doesn't require a per-space license just to turn on
- **Slack or Microsoft Teams integration** , so employees book and check availability without learning a new app
- **Attendance and policy tracking** , so you can see whether hybrid day requirements are being met
- **Usage analytics** , without paying extra to see your own occupancy data
- **Simple, predictable pricing** you can explain in one sentence


## Cost-Effective Alternatives to Microsoft Places


**Officely** is built for exactly this gap. It's a hybrid work and desk booking platform that lives inside Slack and Microsoft Teams, so your team never has to open a separate app to book a desk or plan an office day.


Here's what that looks like in practice:


- **Desk and hot-desk booking** is built in from the start, not an upsell.
- **Hybrid scheduling** lets employees pick office days and lets managers see who's coming in, without a spreadsheet.
- **Neighbourhoods** help teams sit together on the days they're in, so office time stays collaborative.
- **Policy tracking** gives you visibility into whether people are meeting minimum office-day requirements, so hybrid policy stays measurable instead of a guess.
- **Workplace analytics** shows office utilization without a separate reporting license.


Because Officely runs through tools your team already uses, adoption tends to happen on its own. You're not asking people to learn new software; you're asking them to click a button in Slack.


Other tools worth knowing about if you're comparing the market: **deskbird** and **Skedda** focus on desk and room booking with their own standalone apps, while **Robin** , **Envoy** , **OfficeSpace** , **Condeco** , and **Kadence** lean further into room booking, visitor management, or space planning for larger facilities teams. They're worth a look if you need deep real-estate functionality. If you mainly need hybrid scheduling and desk booking without the overhead, that's where Officely is built to fit.


## Why Simplicity Beats "Included"


A feature being bundled into your Microsoft 365 plan doesn't make it free if the parts you need sit behind extra licenses. The real cost of a workplace tool is what it takes to roll out, get people using it, and keep paying for as you scale.


A tool that works inside Slack or Teams from day one skips most of that cost before you even look at a price list.
